input.raw_text: Dear SBI Customer, your YONO Bank account has been BLOCKED due to expired KYC documents. Update your Aadhaar and PAN immediately at https://sbi-kyc-quickupdate.net/verify to restore netbanking and avoid a Rs.5,000 penalty by tonight 9:00 PM.

claim: State Bank of India YONO customer account is blocked due to expired KYC and requires immediate verification via sbi-kyc-quickupdate.net to avoid a 5,000 INR penalty by 9:00 PM.

confidence.rationale: Directly matches documented phishing and smishing scam templates identified by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Cyber Crime portal.

plain_explanation: This message is a fraudulent phishing scam designed to steal your netbanking credentials and OTPs. Banks and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) never send SMS messages containing unverified third-party web links (.net/.xyz) demanding immediate KYC updates or threatening sudden penalty fees with short deadlines.

evidence.source_name: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) - Kehta Hai Campaign
evidence.excerpt: RBI cautions members of the public against sharing OTP, PIN, CVV, or clicking links in SMS/WhatsApp regarding KYC expiration or account suspension.

evidence.source_name: State Bank of India Official Security Advisory
evidence.excerpt: SBI never sends links over SMS asking customers to update KYC. Official KYC updates are conducted strictly through official SBI branches or the official SBI YONO mobile app.

counter_arguments_checked: Are periodic KYC updates required by Indian banking regulations?
Does SBI ever use domain suffixes like .net or .org for customer portals?
edge_cases_identified: While periodic KYC is mandated by RBI guidelines every few years, legitimate notices give multiple months of notice through official registered email/post and never ask for immediate credentials over unverified third-party URLs.
stress_test.robustness_summary: Domain analysis and strict regulatory guidelines confirm this is an adversarial social engineering/smishing attack.

truth_timeline.event: RBI issued circular emphasizing digital re-KYC processes can only be initiated by the customer from within authenticated core banking platforms.
Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) listed sbi-*-update domain patterns in active scam registries.
truth_timeline.significance: Technical threat intelligence confirming phishing infrastructure.

truth_timeline.event: Telecom Regulatory Authority (TRAI) enforced DLT header validation to curb unauthorized SMS spoofing.
truth_timeline.significance: Shows that messages arriving from personal mobile numbers or non-standard sender IDs are unauthorized.

action_risk.warning_flag: DO NOT CLICK: High risk of immediate unauthorized bank account drainage.
action_risk.recommended_action: Do not click the link or enter password/OTP. Block the sender and report the message to the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal at cybercrime.gov.in or helpline 1930.
